content: Individuals diagnosed with type 2 diabetes exhibit a heightened susceptibility to fractures, particularly involving the hip and other major skeletal structures, when compared to individuals without diabetes. Sustained poor glycemic control, defined as an A1C level exceeding 9% over a duration of two years, is strongly associated with a significantly elevated risk of fractures. The use of specific glucose-lowering pharmacological agents, such as thiazolidinediones, has been identified as a contributing factor to an increased likelihood of fractures.
